body:
Closes viola-0.1.0: every gate green on Linux (fmt, clippy, check, test, cargo deny, the deny probes, the tokio-free and release checks, CI's seven jobs), the red supply-chain job fixed by moving portable-pty off =0.8.1 to a release whose graph drops pin-utils, no ignore-list widening.
Removes or keeps with a reason each Windows remnant in code (tests/cli_output_plain.rs, viola-agent-claude, the viola-e2e harness EXE_SUFFIX joins, plain_drive, the coverage-floor comments, host.rs's windows key), the masters following.
Makes the masters agree with the code and each other: decides tool or text for the trycmd / assert_cmd pinned-string claims (no manifest holds either, no tests/cmd/ exists, re-measured at HEAD), the error-enum and thiserror census, the Occupied Resources markers, the obs-plan process-start row.
Re-measures live on Linux, within two headless live sessions on the pty rig: v1-53's one viola run under a driver, a dialog hold near the 3600 s ceiling, the channel-handle no-leak property under the fake agent.
Rules each of the 17 unclaimed caps proved or deferred on the founder's word, and records claims and deferrals in the verification matrix; no new verb, flag, env var, channel method or product surface.

body: The a11y plan's own claims that trycmd / assert_cmd pin the fixed CLI strings: the harness tool pick and keyboard harness (contract keys a11y-testing-tool-pick and keyboard-test-harness), the per-surface reach table's cli row naming assert_cmd 2.2.2, predicates 3.1.4 and trycmd 1.2.1, the CI stage table row, the strategy pyramid's Understandable and Cognitive rows, and the P2 / P6 path scenarios; item 1 decides tool or text for each, so their wording may change here.

The cognitive-accessibility verification lines that name trycmd: error recovery's per-refusal layout pin, plain language's pinned fixed strings (trycmd or literal), and consistency's verification source for the CAPTION order; each is re-worded or kept by item 1's decision.

The reach table's tui row naming the portable-pty outer-PTY boundary driver as inherited `=0.8.1`, and the cli row's portable-pty outer-PTY SGR checks: once the pin moves (item 12) the plan's version text follows the new release.

The tui boundary assertions run on the outer-PTY driver that the portable-pty bump changes: zero viola-originated bytes, human keystrokes delivered unblocked past the current atomic paste, focus / mouse / resize sequences and terminal replies not moving the wheel (path P4, its procedure in the ARIA detail); they must stay green on ubuntu-latest after the bump.

The CLI SGR discipline asserted under the outer PTY, which the bump also reaches: no SGR of viola's own under non-TTY, NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb, --json, viola run or a passed revive; amber only on DIALOG, bold only on NAME values, every SGR span beside its word; dim only on stale rows, proven at the unit tier and under the outer PTY (path P6 and the visual SGR detail).

The plain-mode output discipline that tests/cli_output_plain.rs and plain_drive carry: removing their Windows lines must keep the non-TTY / NO_COLOR / TERM=dumb assertions (no SGR, C0/C1 escaped except newline and tab, linear static output) at their coverage.

The viola run TUI passthrough the live sessions use (v1-53, the hint's driver-drives-a-builder session): viola writes zero bytes to the terminal but the child's output, its run diagnostics go to diagnostics/, human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or delayed; the live reading is a boundary reading only.

The ban on parsing the rendered claude TUI screen or taking screenshots as evidence: the live readings this chunk makes (v1-53's run, the dialog hold, the wheel and tab-close legs) rest on viola's own outputs and the JUnit, never on screen content.

The wheel's non-editing rule (P4 and the Keyboard anti-pattern: focus, mouse, resize sequences and terminal replies never count as human editing): item 10's hypothesis that a terminal answering CSI ? 6 n or the kitty graphics query loses the wheel at start tests exactly this rule; a shape joins the list only when measured, by its exact grammar, on the founder's word.

The timeout rule in cognitive accessibility: the dialog hold is one of viola's time bounds that falls on the driver, never on the human, and no key is blocked by it; reading a hold near the 3600 s ceiling live (item 2) must keep that, and the plan's statement of the hold follows if the ceiling leaves PROVISIONAL.

The CI integration the green-on-Linux clause reads: one ci.yml on the matrix [ubuntu-latest], the CLI output-discipline and TUI boundary cases inside the test job's single instrumented coverage suite, whose gate --require coverage,doctest allows no skip; failures land in the harness run JSON suites[].failures[].

No WCAG conformance claim for the cli or the viola run TUI: the matrix claims this chunk writes for the caps it proves (v1-26's fix-pass surfaces, v1-53, v1-01 and the rest) cite assert_cmd / portable-pty results as output-discipline stand-ins for SC 1.3.2 / 1.4.1 / 3.3.1, not as conformance.

The frontend deferred to 0.2.0 with its technology not chosen: a cap whose acceptance names a surface 0.1.0 does not build (the page, feed or strip bay) is deferred only on the founder's word, and the plan's deferral statement is the reason text it cites.

The CLI board path P6 where item 4 reaches: v1-36's link set on the board, deferred or re-worded, must leave the CAPTION literal's order NAME · LIVE · STATUS · WHEEL · DIALOG · CLI and the board's parity with the deferred 0.2.0 page undrifted.

body: The PTY decision: `portable-pty` pinned behind viola's own `pty` seam (spawn, read, write, resize, wait, kill). It names this entry as the owner of the move off `=0.8.1`. Under the new release, child exit is still detected on the process handle, `pty_backend()` still reads `openpty`, no human key is held behind a resize and DA1 is never answered. The Stack line's `=0.8.1` text follows the move.

The supply-chain surface: RUSTSEC-2026-0441 reaches the tree through `portable-pty =0.8.1` → `nix 0.25.1` → `pin-utils`. It is read by `cargo deny check advisories` and CI's `supply-chain` job, whose `target/supply-chain/` artifact holds `deny.json` and `deny-fuzz.json`. The remedy may not widen the ignore list.

Indirect, through the new `portable-pty` graph: the Tokio containment keystone binds it. The sole-root `cargo deny` `tokio` ban, the `cargo check` of the sync crates in `scripts/sync-crates.txt` (`viola-pty` among them) and the tokio-free channel check must stay green, and so must `deny.toml`'s licence allow list.

Occupied Resources, Environment variables: `MCP_SERVE_TEST_CHILD` is registered there as a test-only marker. `PTY_SIDELOAD_TEST_CASE` is either registered beside it or stated as taking no row, its presence re-measured at HEAD (item 3).

The Error Handling decision and its echoes: one `thiserror` enum per crate, `PtyError` the ratified exception. The open divergences `ServeError`, `StampsError`, `PinError`, `StampsReadError` and `Refused` each take a fold or a ratification. The derive count (nine stated, ten measured) is re-measured and re-worded in architecture fct-gctodeyz, the Conventions error-types line (fct-nhsg4k7g) and the Inherited Defaults Errors line.

The architecture `project-directory-structure` contract key and the masters' trycmd / assert_cmd text pinning CLI strings under `tests/cmd/*.toml`. No manifest holds either tool and no `tests/cmd/` exists: the chunk decides tool or text, the absence re-measured at HEAD.

The dialog hold: `dialog_hold_s` (60–3600 s, default 60) has a PROVISIONAL ceiling owned by this entry, in the Hook Contract decision, `config.json` and `schemas/config.v1.json`. The `timeout` 3615 on the PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks also applies. A hold near the ceiling is read live here.

The Deployment / Distribution decision: the pinned copy `bin/<version>-<hash>/` is keyed by the first 16 hex of the content SHA-256. Measurement B (one tree building two files that differ in `.note.gnu.build-id`, `.symtab` and `.strtab`) is owed to this entry as a founder item.

The Linux-only rule and its Process and path discipline: the Windows and macOS code is out of the tree (tag `multi-os-final`). A gate whose predicate names `windows` or `target_os = "macos"` reads as a fault. Masters that still describe a removed remnant (for example the CLI Conventions' Git Bash rewritten-path warning, which `plain_drive` served) follow the removal.

The `viola-e2e` harness's binary paths (`viola-harness` builds, `target/perf/release/viola`, test bins) and its `run --coverage` floors and ignore regex (`target/lcov.info`). The `run --mutants` cfg-predicate host table, whose `windows` key item 17 names, also applies.

The Linux IPC endpoint: a Unix socket `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` in a per-user 0700 directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` or `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`), chmod 0600, a peer admitted only for the owning euid. The channel-handle no-leak property is measured on it: the wrapped child's `/proc/<child pid>/fd` holds no channel socket or listener. Then security-plan fct-p7rzex2i is re-worded off «recorded, not established».

The mutation audit's survivor: an always-admit `peer_admitted` read at the three client seams survives every committed test. One account makes no foreign peer, and no seam may be added. The survivor stays a dated note at matrix#v1-44 and test-plan §1's untestable zone.

The live-session rule: the real `claude` runs only in local live tests, never in CI. `run --local-live` refuses under `CI` and the `AGENT_RUN_*` harness variables. The live homes sit at `target/e2e-home/viola-live-<pid>/home`. `v1-53`'s claim reads the census and the `ubuntu-latest` JUnit (`target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`) alone.

The driving surfaces the live «overseer drives a builder through viola» session uses: the wrapped start (`viola run <name> -- <program>`), the wheel starting at `driver`, `send` / `wait` / `answer` and the implicit link they record. The MCP tools reach a session as `mcp__plugin_viola_viola__<tool>`.

`v1-13` and `v1-36` take their dispositions here. `link` and `release` (budget included) are CLI-only, so no MCP result exists for them. The `list` payload carries no link set, while the deferred 0.2.0 page's intent names one. Each clause is deferred with its reason or re-worded, on the founder's word.

The Human Takeover / Wheel decision's closed non-editing list, measured on foot 1.28.0 only. A shape joins the list only when measured, by its exact grammar.

Session liveness and the killed-wrapper leg: a real `claude` read on Unix ending with its killed wrapper, and the founder-attended tab-close in a Linux terminal. The fake-agent reading `run_child_ends_when_its_wrapper_is_terminated` stands meanwhile, beside the heartbeat and pid + start-time `gone` rule.

The edit lands through the store's whole-fact form (`@fact id=… expect_rev=N whole=true`), as does removing the seven directory-tree pointer lines from `fct-irhgihut`.

CI/CD: GitHub Actions on `ubuntu-latest` only, its seven jobs (`test`, `perf`, `msrv`, `fuzz-replay`, `lint`, `release`, `supply-chain`) all green at the wrap. Setup's red run ci#42255961371 is closed against its own log. The `release-check` gate refuses an artifact built with `viola-channel`'s `test-support` feature.

The verification matrix's claims and deferrals for the 17 unclaimed caps (`v1-01` … `v1-53`): `v1-01`'s CI-run outcome and advisories clause become provable once the `portable-pty` move lands. A cap whose acceptance names a 0.2.0 surface reads `deferred` only on the founder's word.

body_fields.convention: every OS-gated test names its reason in the census binary `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs`, and a gate predicate naming `windows` or `target_os = "macos"` reads as a fault

every new test runs against the fake agent named after `--` in its own viola home (`--home`, under `target/e2e-home/`), never sharing an endpoint, log or `budget.json`. The real `claude` runs only in local live tests, refused under CI.
a test-only environment marker sits outside the `VIOLA_*` namespace, is read by no `viola` build, and is registered in Occupied Resources → Environment variables

every test-only path or scratch dir (temp-dir reports, `target/` probe and run dirs) is registered in Occupied Resources (Filesystem or Repository), is gitignored when under `target/`, and is never read or written by `viola`

a new log line goes to its role's codes-only process log under `diagnostics/`, in the obs-owned format fixed by `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`. Content-bearing detail goes only to the instance's `diagnostics/detail-<role>.ndjson`.
a test-only feature or binary is never in a release build: it is gated behind its feature (`fake-agent`, `test-support`) and refused by the release check

body: The per-method channel contracts (`params` → `ok` payloads, `from` typing, `MAX_FRAME`, the protocol-fault codes): the chunk adds no verb, flag, env var or channel method and changes no payload.
The `RefusalReason` value set, its detail sets and refusal order, and the CLI exit-code table: no refusal, detail or exit code is added or changed.
The normalised event kinds, the Hook → kind map and the per-kind event `data` shapes: no event kind or field changes.
The snapshot envelope, the instance snapshot's fields and the replay readers: no snapshot field or reader changes.
The ledger stamps envelope, the capability-ledger rows and `viola verify`'s probe plugin and probe dirs: no ledger row or probe is added.
The `hook statusline` contract, `statusline-source.json`, the per-session `settings.json` override and the budget thresholds' defaults: no statusline or budget mechanism changes.
`viola plugin install` and its local marketplace tree: untouched.
`viola revive`: its preflight, `--list` and its `--json` refusal codes are untouched.
The naming and data-model conventions (`ViolaName` grammar, the FNV-1a endpoint-name hash, RFC 3339 timestamps, `Option` field omission, `Percent`): no identifier or wire format changes.
The vt100 readiness gate and the delivery-confirmation window and its `unconfirmable` outcome: not changed.
The snapshot writer's tempfile helpers and the crash-safe write discipline of logs and lock files: no writer changes.
The pins of the other dependencies (clap, chrono, rmcp, interprocess, vt100, tempfile, serde_json, nutype): only `portable-pty` and the graph it brings move.
The Mobile, Hosting and AI/ML rows and the Template patterns: N/A in v1 and unreached.
The R8 identity strip and the `IDENTITY_FLOOR`, and the colour variables `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM`: no environment row of theirs changes.
Protocol versioning (`v`, the sender version) and mixed-version tolerance: no format is added, removed or re-meant.

body: **2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — RUSTSEC-2026-0441 red, owned by «Version done-check» (amd-s2pop7pg): recorded the advisory (`pin-utils` via `portable-pty =0.8.1` → `nix 0.25.1`) red in supply-chain's advisories family at ci#42030025050, owner a CARRY on this entry, remedy fixed as moving `portable-pty` off `=0.8.1` with no ignore-list widening; `portable-pty` kept `=0.8.1` until then. This is item 12's mandate and the record (fct-co2wsjkw) this chunk retires once the move lands.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — [PTY]: openpty alone, the Windows ConPTY host retired (amd-sjbu5y3g): `pty_backend()` always `openpty`, rationale «0.8.1 is spike-proven», the move off it owed to «Version done-check»; the 0.9.0 Windows garbage-read bug that justified the `=0.8.1` pin left with the Windows code; child exit stays on the handle wait; the resize rule (no human key held behind a resize) stands; viola-pty's `sideload` removed, recoverable at `multi-os-final`. The old reason for the pin is gone, so a newer release is open to research; the seam semantics the new release must keep are the ones this entry restated.

**2026-10-26-tokio-rustsec-2026-0386-lock-bump** — the precedent for an advisory remedy: the `[workspace.dependencies]` exact pin moved `tokio` `=1.53.1` → `=1.53.3`, the lock re-resolved to a patched version, `cargo deny check` green with no ignore widened, containment re-read (four sole-root bans, `channel-tokio-free: ok`), and the version text moved in both the Stack row and the Inherited Defaults line. Item 12 follows the same form: one pin, `Cargo.lock` re-resolved, every master site of the version text moved together (Stack PTY row, [PTY] entity, body Stack line).

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — windows-sys out, libc a plain dependency (amd-3vni4ift): new OS bindings Stack row (libc plain in the root, `viola-channel`, `viola-pty`, `viola-state`, `viola-e2e`; no crate on windows-sys); `viola-pty` → portable-pty, tracing, libc, and `PtyError`'s rationale lists exactly those three. The new portable-pty graph must keep this set and must not bring windows-sys back into a viola crate.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** — `PtyError` ratified as the one exception to «thiserror per crate» (hand-written fixed `Display`/`Error`), `viola-pty` landed with no thiserror; portable-pty's error kept as a boxed source. The exception's reason is the seam's exact dependency set, so it must stay true under the moved `portable-pty` (item 6/16 and the PTY binding).

**2026-09-27-wrapper-channel** — `viola-pty` gained tracing, so [Error Handling]'s exact dependency set became the seam's stated set (then portable-pty, tracing, windows-sys, libc). Shows that any dependency change to `viola-pty` re-words [Error Handling]'s `PtyError` rationale in the same pass.

**2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty** — the sideload built on `portable-pty =0.8.1`'s bare-name `conpty.dll` load, and added to the tree `src/conpty.rs`, viola-pty `sideload`, `scripts/conpty-vendor.sh` and `vendor/conpty/<version>/x64/`. These are the origins of the `(removed …; recoverable at the tag multi-os-final)` pointer lines F434 removes from fct-irhgihut, and of the `PTY_SIDELOAD_TEST_CASE` marker item 3 re-measures.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — the ConPTY companions and their vendored binaries retired (amd-df3o7iha): `src/conpty.rs`, `scripts/conpty-vendor.sh`, `vendor/conpty/` marked removed in project-directory-structure, recoverable at `multi-os-final`; `pin_companions`, `PinError::StrictModes`, `seed_conpty` and `run.conpty_sideload` removed; the chaos home the one named test-data carve-out. These marks are the pointer lines F434 now deletes from fct-irhgihut, and `PinError` lost a variant here (item 6's `PinError` disposition reads the enum as it stands now).

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — mutation runs: no scratch arm, no Windows leg (amd-a7hccmy6): project-directory-structure marks `windows-mutants.yml` removed, recoverable at `multi-os-final` (the pointer line with its continuation lines F434 removes); `run --mutants` on Linux alone, the Windows `HOST_SCRATCH` arm deleted. Bears on item 17's `host.rs` `windows` test-host key.

**2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade** — added `harness::run::mutants::host`, the `#[cfg]` reader behind `run --mutants`' host exclusion, with syn `=2.0.119` / proc-macro2 `=1.0.107` as direct dependencies of the test-only `viola-e2e` alone (the Code quality row). This is the `host.rs` whose `windows` test-host key item 17 removes or keeps; the Code quality row (fct-lj7tqt64) names the reader and must follow.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — residual Windows reasons and the one-leg lint job (amd-mz3cgxib): `viola-harness gate` enforces «the coverage floors» (was per-OS), `target/harness/`'s Windows relink reason dropped, the orphans control gated on `cfg(target_os = "linux")`, the root bin's Windows dev-dependency retired; found by a residual census after the sweep (no sweep pattern named those words). The precedent for item 17: remnants a line grep misses, the `COVERAGE_FLOORS` «per OS» comments among them, are found by a residual census, and the masters follow the code.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — the OS-gate census faults a gate naming another OS (amd-7lclwt2z): the body's «Process and path discipline» line, nothing shells out through `sh` or `bash`, and a gate naming `windows` or `target_os = "macos"` reads as a fault (`another OS: …`) even when a `GATES` row names it; the planted Windows cases build the word from a `WINDOWS` const; the new class caught a multi-line `cfg_attr` pair a line grep could not see. Item 17's removals and `v1-53`'s census read are held to this.

**2026-11-04-linux-and-macos-parity** — the OS-gated tests census (amd-wbuntcnq): `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs` with its `GATES` table, failing both ways (an unnamed gate, and a row whose gate no longer stands). Standing rule: a new or removed OS gate moves its `GATES` row in the same change, which item 17's remnant sweep must keep.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — the OS target: Linux only (amd-zmsktnf7): §Design Philosophy, [Scale / Product], §Project Intent and Inherited Defaults CI reworded to Linux only, the Windows and macOS code recoverable at `multi-os-final` (`ecbe7ab3`). This is the rule each item-17 remnant is removed or kept against.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — CI on the one `ubuntu-latest` leg (amd-yr5ehahj): the matrix `[ubuntu-latest]`, workflows 3 → 2, 7 `ci.yml` jobs all green at ci#42030025050 except `supply-chain`, `deny-sync.toml` evaluated for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, coverage at floors 85/95/80. This sets the «every gate green» baseline: `supply-chain` is the one job item 12 must turn green.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — cargo-deny: one Linux triple, one 0BSD exception (amd-35twiter): both deny configs on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`; the 0BSD exceptions narrowed to `doctest-file` alone (a `recvmsg` exception the graph no longer held was dropped, since it narrows and widens nothing). A new portable-pty graph that pulls a crate outside the `allow` list would need a new exception, which counts as widening. A dropped crate may also leave an exception unmatched (`license-exception-not-encountered`).

**2026-09-25-security-prerequisites** — the licence `allow` list and the per-crate 0BSD exceptions recorded in Dependency policy, «never through `allow`», an operator-ratified boundary widening. The remedy must hold the list exactly (MIT, Apache-2.0, Zlib, Unicode-3.0 + one 0BSD exception) and add nothing.

**2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates** — the tokio ban became `deny-sync.toml` run once per crate in `scripts/sync-crates.txt` as the sole root. The reason: `--exclude` false-fails under feature unification, which falsified the excluded-graph mechanism. This is the origin of the anti-pattern the extract binds, and the ban the new `viola-pty` graph must pass.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** — the Tokio client and viola-channel's tree-form ban (amd-yawcyqfu): the sync crates of `scripts/sync-crates.txt` are four (`viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`), `viola-channel` off the list and proven by `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`. A premise ("covered through the sync roots") was corrected by measurement. Job 3's set and the supply-chain tokio steps re-run after the portable-pty move are this set.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — the serde_json `unbounded_depth` ban and the deny probe count (amd-5ws2khmo): `deny-probes: 14/14 banned, control clean`, the count one per `probes=(` row plus the planted `channel-tokio-edge`, every master site moved together. This is the probe verdict the acceptance re-reads after the remedy. Its rule changes only if a probe row is added.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — bounded readers, a cross-cutting pattern held by a census (amd-ifvkvtl4): every product reader of external bytes is bounded in its statement or named in `EXCEPTIONS` of `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs`. If the new `portable-pty` API reshapes a reader in `crates/viola-pty`, it must stay bounded or be named, or the census goes red.

**2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows** — Run E's resources and a killed PTY child's exit status (amd-mb4bcuuw): a child of an interactive PTY run killed at a Ctrl-C/TERM stop closes with a `child_exit_status`, since portable-pty reports a code for a signalled child, as measured by the resume-run stop case. The moved portable-pty must keep this behaviour, or the occupied-resources diagnostics sentence (fct-6oxorhgk) is false.

**2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton** — toolchain floor and exact pin (amd-k6bajxtn): `rust-version = "1.96"` the declared floor, Rust 1.98.1 pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`. The new portable-pty graph must build at 1.96 so that the `msrv` job stays green with neither floor nor pin moved.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — the CI `msrv` check (rustup 1.96 + `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`, which outranks `rust-toolchain.toml`) recorded in the runtime row. This is the job that judges the floor for the moved graph.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — the enum census: `Refusal` folded, `CoreError` out, five open divergences (amd-eixrfzzz): `Refusal` folded into `AgentError` (not ratified, `StampError` the precedent, outputs unchanged); open divergences `ServeError`, `StampsError` plus the census's `PinError`, `StampsReadError`, `Refused`, owner a CARRY on «Version done-check»; 9 `thiserror::Error` derives by `command grep -rn "thiserror::Error" src crates --include=*.rs`, stated in Rust error types. These are item 6's five divergences and item 16's count (now reading 10), and the census command is the one to re-measure with.

**2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness** — StampError folded into AgentError; Refusal named the open divergence (amd-mcf4uu6e): a second enum in one crate folded into the crate enum as a new variant (`StampsMalformed`), the one-enum rule standing. This is the fold precedent for each of item 6's divergences.

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** — `StampError` named an interim divergence, not an exception. The overseer ruled that the locked one-enum rule stands and the fold rides the route as a CARRY. This shows that a divergence is folded unless the ruling owner ratifies it as an exception.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** — ServeError, a second open divergence (amd-6ngwtzjn): `viola-mcp` holds `ServeError` (`Runtime`, `Initialize`, `Session`; fixed messages, returned by `serve`) beside `McpError`; recorded open, its fold or ratification owed. This is item 6's first divergence.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — `viola mcp`'s exit on a stdin cut before `initialize` (amd-hvmzy5yr): `ServeError::Initialize` exits 1 (was stated 11, disproved by measurement); 11 is only the unit child's own code (`serve_child_entry`). A fold of `ServeError` into `McpError` must keep these exits and the one `parse-rejected{mcp-stdin}` line.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — [MCP] the viola mcp stdin line cap (amd-tt7t6u67): `serve` returns `ServeError::Initialize` when a cut lands before `initialize`, writing one `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin"}` line; no error variant was added. This is a behaviour a `ServeError` fold has to carry unchanged.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** — the stamps writer's strict-modes check; StampsError, a third open divergence (amd-7bepytvq): `update_stamps` runs `check_stamps` before it creates `ledger/` and again under its lock, refusing as `StampsError::StrictModes` (`StrictModes` · `State`, fixed messages), which `verify` maps to the home pair. A fold of `StampsError` must re-word this text, the ledger-stamps contract and the occupied-resources `ledger/stamps.json` line together.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** — the read rule and check_instance's widened set (amd-uiudhtfc): `Refused` holds `Readable` and `Symlink`, each with a fixed message. This is the origin of the `Refused` enum, the census's fifth divergence.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** — the socket-directory check's read and its home in the code (amd-duanemqw): `check_socket_dir` (one `symlink_metadata`; `Refused::Unreadable`, `Symlink`, fixed-message `NotADirectory`; never chmods, a refused directory left as found); no check inside `viola_channel::Client::connect`, since `viola-channel` has no `viola-state` edge. `viola list` carries no link column in v1 and its six columns stay fixed (Iconography and the cli-list patterns): v1-36's clause «link set on the board» is deferred or re-worded against this, and the master text must agree with whichever the founder rules.

`viola link` / `viola unlink` output phraseology and the `viola release <name> --budget` line (cli-verbs), with `mcp` as a hidden verb writing MCP frames only (Platform-Specific Notes): v1-13's clause on the MCP result for `link` and the budget release is deferred or re-worded against these.

The colour decision order (`--json`, `viola run`, `hook` / `mcp`, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, non-terminal stdout) and the plain-output contract: removing the remnants in `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` and `plain_drive` must leave every plain-mode output and its assertions unchanged.

The cli Platform-Specific Notes' Git Bash on Windows rewritten-path warning: where an item 17 remnant removal reaches that warning, the design-system line follows (removed, or kept with its reason) as one of the masters following.

The cli Platform line (Linux terminals, CI on `ubuntu-latest`): the version done-check's «every gate green on Linux» and `v1-53`'s `ubuntu-latest` JUnit read sit on this platform statement, which must still agree once the remnants leave.

Indirect, through the `Cargo.toml` edit: clap stays built without its `color` feature and no added or moved dependency reads a colour or terminal variable, so every styled byte stays the SGR module's own; the `portable-pty` move adds no dependency to the `viola` bin's styling.

Indirect, through the `portable-pty` / `crates/viola-pty` move: `viola run` (and a passed `viola revive`) prints nothing once the child starts and emits no colour, glyph or cursor control, the terminal belonging to the child's screen; the new pty release must keep that passthrough.

Indirect, through item 6's enum folds or ratifications (`ServeError`, `McpError`, `StampsError`, `StateError`, `PinError`, `StampsReadError`, `Refused`): the typed exit codes, their human stderr forms, the `--json` `error` / `refusal` documents and the closed `detail` words stay exactly as the exit-code phraseology states; stack traces never print and detail goes to `diagnostics/` only.

body_fields.why: A live hold near the ceiling ends on an answer or at the hold's end, and the read must tell the wrapper's expiry from the hook's 3605 s backstop.

A hand-back or an answer writes neither, and a failed append changes nothing else. The hook writes `deadline_hit:true` only when its own read times out at its backstop bound, `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s).

Indirect, through the `portable-pty` bump: the PTY seam boundary wrapper still gives `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` on spawn, the child's `process-exit` from the handle-wait thread (never reader EOF), `exit_source:"kill-fallback"` on the kill fallback, and paste as `text_bytes` only; the killed-wrapper reading of item 11 rests on that exit path.

The CI gates re-run green at the wrap: G1 bare `#[instrument]`, G2 zero panics, G3 no abort panic strategy, G4 schema conformance against `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` and `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`, the secret scan, and the gated `diag-<os>` / `harness-<os>` / `junit-<os>` uploads in their step order.

The live sessions (v1-53's `viola run`, the overseer driving a builder): `run` writes nothing to the terminal while the child runs and logs to `diagnostics/run-<name>.ndjson`; its evidence is read through `agent-run logs` / `status` and `jq`, never by human review.

The dialog hold near the 3600 s ceiling read live: the dialog → `answer` scenario's lines (a dialog hook's `hook-invoked` written after the `hook.dialog` response, question, answer and tool input never logged) are the read's evidence.

The multi-platform-exporter-compat trigger and the CI platform matrix `[ubuntu-latest]`: one file sink and one line schema on Linux; the remnant removal leaves no OS-specific exporter, artifact or gate branch behind.

The socket-directory refusal pair's wording (a founder item of Epoch 7): the §3 harness contract's start refusals and the `socket-dir-refused` detail code it carries, as that wording is ratified or re-worded.

The `host.rs` `windows` test-host key sits in the mutation harness: a surviving mutant in obs code at `run --mutants` is a build failure, and the mutation audit's one survivor by construction (`peer_admitted`) keeps its dated note and untestable zone.

body_fields.why: crates/viola-pty is reached whole by the portable-pty move, so host_size must still never yield a zero size and the PTY output must still feed vt100 under catch_unwind with passthrough unblocked.
body_fields.quote: Feed through `std::panic::catch_unwind`: a tee on `run`'s pump output writes the human's bytes first and hands a copy to a feed thread, which runs every feed and resize under the catch. A caught panic poisons the screen model until the host size changes, with one `parse-rejected{parser:"vt100-feed", detail:"panicked"}` line per poisoning and no screen text; a poisoned model reads `input-not-ready`, which confirmed `send` reports as `not-delivered`/`input-not-ready`, and byte passthrough to the human terminal continues. vt100 0.16.2 panics are reachable at real small sizes (as measured at chunk 2026-10-04-readiness-gate-and-timing-constants: a 24×1 screen + a wide character; 1×1 `?u`; 1×2 `abc`); `viola_pty::host_size` never yields a zero size.

PTY output bytes (vt100) — fed under `catch_unwind`, the human's bytes written first; a caught panic or a dropped copy poisons the screen model, which then reads `input-not-ready`, while byte passthrough to the human terminal continues; the feed queue is bounded and a full queue never blocks the passthrough.

body_fields.quote: NEVER let `config.json`, a `VIOLA_*` environment variable or a CLI flag switch off any control in this plan: the socket-directory check, the peer or server verification, the home strict-modes check or `validate_paste_text`. Environment variables are not a configuration channel (architecture.md Cross-cutting Patterns: Config management), and `VIOLA_DIR` is set by a child any same-session agent can influence. The two carve-outs are the test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (capped at 5 s; Decisions Log 2026-09-27) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (fires only on the exact value `1`, a forced fail-open `hook` panic; Decisions Log 2026-09-28): each exists only under `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")`, is absent from every release build and switches off nothing (§Input Validation). NEVER add another such seam or environment read, let these reach a release build, or let a colour fact change a control or reach a log line, error or refusal, without its own Decisions Log entry.
The carve-outs, the two test-only seams and the terminal colour facts, switch off nothing; NEVER add another such seam or environment read without its own Decisions Log entry.

body_fields.quote: NEVER let a test-side removal under `target/e2e-home` take anything but a dir the test side itself created: the root fixture chain's owner sweep and a test home's drop (by `owner.json` record, by its own `TempDir`) and harness `cleanup` (by the `viola-session-` name). On the Linux dev host that path is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so these creations and removals reach outside the working directory: a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (live, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, after it was shown to him as creating and deleting outside the working directory through the link; relayed by the overseer). The two keepers (`prepare_home_base` in `tests/support/home.rs`, `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` in the harness) NEVER follow a linked base unless its target is absolute and one `lstat` of it reads a real directory with no group or other bit; a target that is itself a link is refused, so is a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), and a refusal is a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts). They create the target with mode 0700 through the directory builder (never a chmod after, never a parent) and remove nothing.

NEVER let a test-side removal under `target/e2e-home` take anything but a dir the test side itself created; its two keepers NEVER follow a linked base unless its target is absolute and an owner-only real directory, create the target 0700 and remove nothing; `viola` itself never reads or writes the backing by that name.

Indirect, through the portable-pty bump: the pinning rule (every third-party root-graph version pinned exactly in workspace.dependencies, Cargo.lock committed) and the critical-CVE response path (bump, or swap along the named portable-pty-psmux 0.9.7 path) govern how the new version is chosen and recorded.

Indirect, through the new portable-pty graph: the deny.toml licence allow list stays exact (any new non-listed licence crate needs its own per-crate exception and Decisions Log entry), sources stay crates.io only, the C-building crate bans and the sync-crate tokio bans (deny-sync, channel-tokio-free, deny probes) must still pass with the new transitive crates.

Channel handle inheritance: the measurement that the wrapped child's /proc/<child pid>/fd holds no channel socket or listener on Linux under the fake agent, and the ban on inheritable channel handles; any portable-pty move must keep the close-on-exec property; the Data Protection handle-inheritance line is re-worded by this chunk off recorded-not-established.

Indirect, through crates/viola-pty's spawn after the bump: viola run must still hand portable-pty an absolute child path it resolved itself (child executable resolution), and the vt100 feed must stay under catch_unwind with byte passthrough unblocked.

Error Handling's product error enum list (PtyError hand-written; AgentError, ChannelError, StateError, PinError, StampsError, StampsReadError, Refused, McpError, ServeError via thiserror) with fixed-message Display impls: the one-enum-per-crate folds or ratifications and the thiserror derive census re-measure (10 vs 9) may change the enum set the list names; a PtyError change from the portable-pty bump keeps no upstream text or path in Display.

The gates the chunk must bring green: CI's cargo deny job over all four families plus the fuzz/Cargo.lock advisories and sources step, the release check (scripts/release-check.sh refusing test-only features fake-agent and test-support, its probe 5/5), zizmor on the workflows, the G2 zero-panics gate with its one FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC exemption, and the artifact canary secret scan gating uploads.

The live sessions (at most two, headless pty rig, no human key, no window): the real claude resolved from the calling PATH as an accepted same-user risk; a driver driving a wrapped builder over MCP or the CLI through the channel's existing peer and server-verification checks; every recorded reading kept free of CLAUDE* stripped values, user content and absolute paths (NEVER-log floor).

The accepted residual for a scratch reading of a newer CLI: such a live start is no standing permission, each further reading needs its own answer; the dev-host prerequisite for a real-CLI run from a trusted folder.
The dialog hold ceiling (3600 s, PROVISIONAL until a hold near it is read live): config values never make the dialog hold zero or unbounded; the hold is read, not reconfigured.

The human-terminal vector: the stdin classifier's closed non-editing list (the wheel) is extended only by a reply measured live by its exact grammar on the founder's word, never on a guess (the CSI ? 6 n and kitty graphics hypothesis).

Test-only env markers: whether PTY_SIDELOAD_TEST_CASE still exists at HEAD and takes an Occupied Resources row beside MCP_SERVE_TEST_CHILD; the rule that no new test seam or environment read is added without its own Decisions Log entry, and that test seams are compiled out of release and switch off no control.

The mutation audit's survivor: an always-admit peer_admitted read at the three client seams (the client's own-euid peer admission in server verification) stays untested by construction; no seam may be added to reach it, matrix#v1-44 and test-plan section 1 holding the note.

Measurement B (one tree keying two bin/<key>/ folders, unequal .note.gnu.build-id, .symtab, .strtab): the pinned binary keyed by its content hash, re-hashed (SHA-256) before reuse; the chunk records the founder item and acts on it only by his word.

The founder's word owed on the socket-directory pair's wording (the per-user 0700 directory, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/ or /tmp/viola-<uid>/) and on the board's read rule (list rows, unwrapped rows from claude agents --json printed through escape_row).

v1-13 and v1-36 dispositions: link, unlink and release stay off the MCP tool list (an affordance, not an enforcement) and no new channel method, verb or listener is added; the clauses are deferred or re-worded, not built.

Indirect, through the e2e harness edits under crates/viola-e2e/src/harness: a test-side removal under target/e2e-home takes only a dir the test side created, its keepers never following a linked base unless absolute and owner-only.

body: **2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — advisories red on RUSTSEC-2026-0441, owned by Version done-check: added the two dependency-security rows this chunk discharges (the red through `portable-pty =0.8.1` → `nix 0.25.1` → `pin-utils 0.1.0`, the remedy a move off `=0.8.1` to a release whose graph drops `pin-utils`, no ignore widened, the `[advisories]` list keeping its one entry; and the pin carrying no Windows reason, portable-pty 0.9.0's Windows garbage-read bug reaching no code viola builds). Item 12 retires both rows by measurement; the owner was the overseer's technical answer plus the operator's word, not the founder's.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — handle inheritance without the Windows mechanism: the `CreateProcessW bInheritHandles = 0` and `inheritable(false)` mechanism was cut, and the line now reads close-on-exec on Linux «recorded, not established», with the `/proc/<child pid>/fd` measurement under the fake agent owed to a CARRY on «Version done-check» (overseer, founder-delegated, 2026-11-06 16:25Z). The ban shrank to «NEVER make channel handles inheritable». Item 15 is that measurement, and it must be taken on the moved portable-pty graph before fct-p7rzex2i is re-worded.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — the IPC endpoint is a Unix socket alone: retired the Windows pipe's `inheritable(false)` and DACL controls, leaving `<dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` or `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`, never the `/tmp` root, chmod 0600 after the bind. This is the wording of the socket-directory pair the founder's word (item 7) must confirm, and the listener is the descriptor the item 15 fd measurement must not find in the child.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — one licence exception and one deny target triple: `0BSD` now has one per-crate exception (`doctest-file`, through interprocess 2.4.4); added the rule that an exception naming a crate absent from the graph is dropped (`license-exception-not-encountered`). The `deny-sync.toml` tokio ban now runs for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` alone. The portable-pty move must re-run this check: drop any exception the new graph no longer reaches, and give any new non-`allow` licence its own exception and Decisions Log entry.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — CI runs one ubuntu-latest leg: `ci.yml` on `[ubuntu-latest]` with `${{ matrix.os }}` names kept, `windows-mutants.yml` and the mutation-scratch ban retired, zizmor `concurrency-limits` at 2 low findings, and the Windows/macOS code recoverable at tag `multi-os-final` (`ecbe7ab3`). The companion «one-leg CI jobs» entry dropped «per-OS» from the `release`/`perf` lines and kept chmod-after-bind as a reason from the macOS era. Every gate green at wrap is read against this CI shape, and the item 17 remnant removal must keep it true.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — client server verification is one Linux flow: `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own)` admits only `observed == Some(own)`; `SERVER_PID_REPORTED`/`PEER_EUID_REPORTED` folded; the frame ban reads the socket-directory, pid, start-time and euid checks, none skipped, no carve-out. This is the shape the item 8 `peer_admitted` survivor record and the live driver session go through.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — child program resolution is a given path or a bare name on PATH: `resolve_program`'s one refusal is `AgentError::ProgramNotFound`, `BatchScriptChild` and the `.cmd`/`.bat` ban retired, `revive --json` codes 11 → 10, verify's refusal codes 6 → 5. After the portable-pty bump, `viola-pty` must still be handed this absolute path, and `AgentError` is one of the derive-census enums item 16 re-measures.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — the ConPTY sideload and its vendored binaries retired: `pty_backend()` is always `openpty`, the `sideload_fallback` codes are gone, `PinError::StrictModes` left Error Handling, and only the pinned binary is re-hashed. This grounds the item 14 obs-plan `process-start` re-wording (`pty_backend` `openpty` alone, `sideload_fallback` gone). `PinError` is one of the item 6 divergences, so its remaining variants are what a fold or ratification rests on.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — the R8 strip and the fixture scrub match names exactly: every inherited `CLAUDE*` name is stripped except `claude_env_keep`, the eleven-name identity floor always stripped, and the registry reader is retired. The live `viola run` sessions (v1-53, the overseer-drives-builder session) rest on this strip, so evidence must carry no R8-stripped value.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — verify's stop and the colour decision lose their Windows arms: the feed-panic witness now reads the child's bytes reaching the outer terminal with no OS limit, and the colour facts lost the Windows VT enable. This bears on the vt100 `catch_unwind`/passthrough property the portable-pty move must keep, and on the colour-fact carve-out, which the remnant removal must not widen.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — the home strict-modes check is owner and mode alone: the Windows DACL arm and the `NotFound` exception were retired, and the board's read rule and `check_path` hold with no «every OS» qualifier, «the OPEN on the board's read rule unchanged». The founder's word on the board's read rule (item 7) lands on this as-built text and closes or keeps that OPEN.

**2026-11-04-linux-and-macos-parity** — the macOS carve-out's tests named in the census: introduced `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs` and its `GATES` table, which gives every OS-gated test a reason. v1-53's claim reads this census (39 functions, 2 gated files), and a remnant removal under item 17 must keep or justify each gate, e.g. `tests/security_negatives_socket_dir.rs` `#![cfg(unix)]`.

**2026-10-26-tokio-rustsec-2026-0386-lock-bump** — the RUSTSEC-2026-0386 supply-chain red closed: the direct precedent for item 12. An open-advisory item owned by a route entry was retired whole once an exact-pin bump in `[workspace.dependencies]` plus the lock moved the crate to a patched version: `cargo deny check` (all four families, cargo-deny 0.20.2) exited 0, `deny.toml` was untouched and no ignore was widened. RUSTSEC-2017-0008 is restated as the only ignore. A companion entry re-worded the tokio pin and re-read `channel-tokio-free: ok` and the deny probes after the bump.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — serde_json's `unbounded_depth` banned in `deny.toml`, and the deny-probes verdict at 14/14 with its counting rule named (the `probes=(` rows of `scripts/deny-probes.sh` plus the planted `channel-tokio-edge` probe). The deny probes re-run after the portable-pty move must read this verdict. Any change in the count must re-word it with the rule beside the number.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** — the tokio ban's tree form and the rmcp release-graph gate: `viola-channel` left `scripts/sync-crates.txt` and is covered by `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`; lint gained `scripts/rmcp-features.sh` (rmcp exactly `server` + `transport-io` in `viola`'s release graph), and supply-chain runs the tree form after the sole-root loop. Both gates must still pass over the new portable-pty transitive crates.

**2026-10-16-remove-the-browser-leg** — the npm graph, the Node pin, the axum ban and the GUI scan forms left. `[[bans.features]]` held the rmcp ban alone (serde_json was added later), every remaining ban still proven live, and the canary scan's classes were narrowed. This sets the deny-ban set and the secret-scan classes CI must read green against. The 2026-10-20 Epoch 5 batch entry recorded the axum ban and the GUI scan forms as «a separate founder item».

**2026-09-25-security-prerequisites** — 0BSD per-crate exceptions: established the rule that `allow` stays `["MIT", "Apache-2.0", "Zlib", "Unicode-3.0"]` and that each further exception needs its own Decisions Log entry, never an `allow` addition. It was a boundary widening ratified by the overseer, founder-delegated. Any new licence the portable-pty move pulls in falls under this rule.

**2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates** — trust boundary, CI jobs, deny.toml additions, nightly.yml: named `deny.toml`'s four families plus the sole-root `deny-sync.toml` tokio ban as the supply-chain trust boundary, recorded that `scripts/deny-probes.sh` proves every ban live, and set the weekly `nightly.yml` advisory run. This is the gate set the item 12 move must keep green.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — fuzz lockfile exemption: `fuzz/` is a separate workspace outside root `cargo deny`, a test-only exemption that holds only while it never links and never joins the root `[workspace]`, with both lockfiles committed. The follow-up entry 2026-09-24-workspace-tree-and-code-graph-planes wired the `supply-chain` step `Fuzz lockfile audit (advisories, sources)` and the nightly fuzz advisories, and added the per-OS release build through `scripts/release-check.sh` to the CI job list. CI green at wrap includes both.

**2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton** — pinned actions and toolchain source: set the SHA-pinned action set and `rustup toolchain install` from `rust-toolchain.toml`, and ruled that event-payload values reach steps only through `env:`. body_fields.quote: `--exit-no-eof` (a bounded re-exec holder keeps the child's console / PTY slave open for 10 s — not viola's stdout — writes a `hold` receipt, and on Unix spawns in its own process group)

on Unix every command it spawns (each hook, and the status line command) runs in a process group of its own (`process_group(0)`, as the `--exit-no-eof` holder does): its PTY's foreground group is what a hangup of that terminal reaches, at the agent's exit as its session leader or when a killed wrapper closes the PTY, and a `viola hook` reached in its exit-time coverage write leaves a cut-short profile (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup/evidence/profraw-cause.md`). The agent itself, its PTY's session leader, cannot leave that group (`setpgid` refuses a leader), so on Unix its exit ignores SIGHUP from its first step (`\x03` or stdin's end)

body:
The version done-check that closes viola-0.1.0 on Linux. It is mechanism and record work, with no new verb, flag, env var or channel method.
It moves portable-pty off =0.8.1 to a release whose graph drops pin-utils, clearing RUSTSEC-2026-0441 in cargo deny and CI's supply-chain job without widening the ignore list.
It removes the Windows code remnants of freight item 17, or keeps each one with its reason, and the masters follow.
It re-measures at HEAD the missing trycmd/assert_cmd tests/cmd, PTY_SIDELOAD_TEST_CASE, the thiserror derive census and the channel-handle no-leak property under /proc/<child pid>/fd, and it runs up to two headless live sessions (v1-53's live viola run on Linux and a driver driving a builder through viola).
It re-reads every gate green: fmt, clippy, check, test, cargo deny, deny probes, tokio-free checks, release check and CI's seven jobs. It also records a proved or deferred disposition for each of the 17 unclaimed caps, on the founder's word.

body: The supply-chain coverage trigger and the CI supply-chain job. cargo deny runs over the root and fuzz lockfiles, its only ignore is RUSTSEC-2017-0008, and the weekly nightly advisories re-run comes back clean. The portable-pty move has to clear RUSTSEC-2026-0441 inside these rules.

The viola-pty entity and its seam over portable-pty, which the plan pins at =0.8.1. The seam keeps six methods, exit is read from the process handle and never from reader EOF, and consumers are tested against a mockall double. The new portable-pty release must keep all of this, and the plan's version text follows the new pin.

The Module-to-PTY integration boundary. It covers real openpty spawns of the fake agent through viola-pty, exit detected on the handle, a resize propagated, and a key written after a resize. A dependency move under viola-pty must keep these green.

The lint gates must stay green: fmt, clippy -D warnings, the tokio-free cargo check of each crate listed in scripts/sync-crates.txt, the cargo-modules orphans gate and its probe, and the rmcp release-graph assertion.
The supply-chain build-failure lines must stay green: deny-probes 14/14 banned with a clean control, the sole-root tokio ban per sync crate, channel-tokio-free ok, and zizmor.
The release-build line, release-check: viola only, with its probes 5/5 refused and a clean control. The MSRV 1.96 job and the fuzz corpus replay are also among the seven CI jobs that must read green.

The coverage gate in the test job on ubuntu-latest: lines 85, functions 95 and regions 80. COVERAGE_IGNORE's separator-agnostic regex over its four trees stays unwidened while its Windows-path comment is reworded or removed. COVERAGE_FLOORS and the plan's per-OS coverage wording follow item 17.

The multi-os-compat trigger: the product is Linux-only, and the census in tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs treats any gate whose predicate names windows or macos as a fault. Removing remnants must leave the census count and its gated files consistent.
The viola --help literal HELP in tests/cli_output_plain.rs, which pins the human layout. Editing that file's Windows remnants must keep the literal assertion holding.
The harness pieces the EXE_SUFFIX joins sit in, such as the session record and boot paths: each harness command still prints one JSON document and exits 0, 1 or 2 after the joins go.

Item 1 (tool or text). The plan names trycmd 1.2.1 case files as the human-mode layout driver, trycmd only in verify mode, and trycmd cases with snapbox redactions as the expected output. No tests/cmd exists and no manifest holds trycmd, so the masters-agree check decides between the tool and the text, and the plan's wording follows.

The test-child markers MCP_SERVE_TEST_CHILD and PTY_SIDELOAD_TEST_CASE. Each one either gets a row in architecture's Occupied Resources or has the absence explained, and PTY_SIDELOAD_TEST_CASE's presence at HEAD is re-measured.
The DialogHold bounds of 60 to 3600 s in its unit cases, with a 60 s default. The 3600 s ceiling stays PROVISIONAL until a hold near it is read live in one of this chunk's live sessions.

The untestable zone for the real claude CLI. A live reading is the route entry's own local measurement, kept in its evidence/ with its own launcher, driver and readers, never a test layer or a CI step. A green fake-agent run is never proof of real-CLI behaviour. Both live sessions sit inside this rule.

v1-53's claim reads the census and the ubuntu-latest JUnit alone (target/nextest/ci/junit.xml, the junit artifact of the test job). CI conclusions are read with gh run view --json jobs, and artifacts are fetched with gh run download. v1-01's CI-run outcome and advisories clause are read the same way.

The fake agent's Unix behaviour that v1-53's live run confirms. On Unix every command it spawns runs in its own process group, and its exit ignores SIGHUP from the first step. The fake-agent reading run_child_ends_when_its_wrapper_is_terminated also stands for item 11.

The channel-handle no-leak property. The IPC trigger requires no inherited channel handles in the child, the fake agent writes an fds receipt kind, and the E2 scenario says the child holds no viola socket. Item 15 measures this on Linux through /proc/<child pid>/fd under the fake agent.

The cross-OS-user untestable zone for item 8. An always-admit peer_admitted mutant at the three client seams survives every committed test, and no seam may be added. The plan's section 1 holds it as the untestable zone, and matrix v1-44 holds the dated note.

The MCP tool list of exactly send, wait, last, answer and list, never release or link. The E3 link/unlink scenario has its CLI halves built. Together they are why v1-13's MCP link and budget-release clauses and v1-36's board link set need a deferral or a reworded acceptance.

The wheel's closed non-editing list, behind Path 5's human-input wheel flip. A shape joins it only when measured by its exact grammar on a live terminal with a real claude, on the founder's word (item 10).

The test-plan's own Windows wording, which follows item 17's remnant removal: the per-OS session-end perf row, the Windows dev-host perf reading, the identity floor measured on the Windows host, the Windows ConPTY EOF source on viola-pty, and the Windows-path note on the coverage regex.

The socket-directory verdict tests and the board's read rule (list refusing a home another user may read). Item 7 asks the founder's word on the socket-directory pair's wording and on the board's read rule.

The pinned copy's SHA-256 16-hex re-hash and its key under bin/<key>/. Measurement B (item 5) found one tree keying two folders through unequal build-id, symtab and strtab sections. Acting on that finding is the founder's call.

The process-start diagnostics line. obs-plan's row narrows pty_backend to openpty and drops sideload_fallback, and the schema conformance step (gate G4 against diag-line.v1.json) must still pass every home-level diagnostics line.

the product is Linux-only; a new test gate naming windows or macos is a census fault
any workflow change keeps permissions {} at the top, contents read per job, every uses SHA-pinned, rust-cache as the only cache, and no concurrency block
no test or CI step runs the real claude CLI; real-CLI readings are local live measurements only
